neighbours.label: A subject just after a fronted phrase or clause opener ('Hoping to ..., the City', 'Once the Government', 'Last month, the New York Times'); the same names as objects stay lower, on a broad pole.
fire: Hoping to save the old pier, the City of Boston bought it.
Once the Government of Kenya set its budget, it called us.
Last week, the Washington Post ran the story.
With the energy that marked all his work, Larson began again.
Before the FBI was founded, local police did this.
Hoping to win votes, the Governor of Texas cut taxes.
After months of talks, the Bank of Japan agreed.
Years later, the Boston Globe printed a correction.
quiet: Our firm sold the pier to the City of Boston.
Their budget was printed by the Government of Kenya.
Most of us read the Washington Post at home.
The new book was written by Larson.
Local police work with the FBI.
She shook hands with the Governor of Texas.
They went to the Bank of Japan.
My aunt reads the Boston Globe.

notes: Probes: 0.47-0.72 (' it' 0.24); the same names elsewhere 0.13-0.39, so near misses are at risk, and a broad pole (2.3%) makes that likelier. ' he', ' she', ' they' and 'We' are in the card's top examples and are not tested here. The output direction on this pole promotes ' needed', ' required', ' used'.
